title: ML From Scratch
tagline: A ground-up machine learning curriculum for engineers with no maths background.

phases.title: Foundations
phases.subtitle: the maths, built in code
phases.blurb: All of machine learning stands on four ideas: vectors, matrix multiplication, the derivative, and probability. Learn these properly and the rest of the field is recombination. We learn them by writing them, not by reading proofs.
phases.milestone: Minimise a function you have never seen before, from scratch, and explain every line.

lessons.title: Vectors and the dot product
lessons.summary: Python and NumPy essentials, what a vector really is, and the single operation that everything else is built from.

lessons.title: Vector geometry
lessons.summary: Length, distance, angle, cosine similarity, projection. Why 'similarity' turns out to be a geometry problem.

lessons.title: Matrices as data
lessons.summary: Shape, indexing, slicing, broadcasting, transpose. Thinking in two dimensions without loops.

lessons.title: Matrices as transformations
lessons.summary: Matrix multiplication as a function that moves space. This is the one that makes neural networks click.

lessons.title: Systems, inverses, and rank
lessons.summary: Solving Ax = b, the cases where you cannot, and what 'singular' actually means.

lessons.title: Functions and slopes
lessons.summary: The derivative discovered numerically, in code, before a single symbol of calculus notation.

lessons.title: Derivative rules
lessons.summary: Power, product and quotient rules — and the handful of derivatives you will actually reuse forever.

lessons.title: The chain rule
lessons.summary: The most important single fact in deep learning. Backpropagation is the chain rule and nothing more.

lessons.title: Partial derivatives and the gradient
lessons.summary: Calculus in many dimensions, and what it means to point downhill in 4096-dimensional space.

lessons.title: Gradient descent
lessons.summary: Implement it, watch it converge, then deliberately break it and learn why it diverged.

lessons.title: Probability I
lessons.summary: Random variables, distributions, expectation and variance — the language uncertainty is written in.

lessons.title: Probability II
lessons.summary: Bayes' theorem, likelihood, and the derivation of where loss functions actually come from.

lessons.title: The statistics you need
lessons.summary: The normal distribution, sampling, correlation, and the traps that catch practitioners.

phases.title: Classical Machine Learning
phases.subtitle: where every core concept is easiest to see
phases.blurb: Most industry ML is still this. It is also where loss, overfitting, evaluation and regularisation are visible in two dimensions, before deep learning hides them behind a billion parameters.
phases.milestone: Take a raw, messy CSV to a validated and honestly-evaluated model, and defend every choice you made.

lessons.title: What 'learning' actually is
lessons.summary: The universal recipe underneath every model in this repository: data, model, loss, optimiser.

lessons.title: Linear regression from scratch
lessons.summary: Both routes: the closed-form solution, and gradient descent. Then why anyone bothers with the second.

lessons.title: Making training work
lessons.summary: Feature scaling, learning rates, and how to debug a model that will not converge.

lessons.title: Logistic regression
lessons.summary: The sigmoid, decision boundaries, and cross-entropy loss — classification from first principles.

lessons.title: Overfitting and the bias-variance tradeoff
lessons.summary: Train/validation/test, cross-validation, and why your model looked brilliant right up until it shipped.

lessons.title: Regularisation
lessons.summary: L1 and L2, and a real intuition for why penalising large weights makes a model generalise.

lessons.title: Evaluation
lessons.summary: Accuracy is a trap. Precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC and confusion matrices, and when each one lies.

lessons.title: scikit-learn
lessons.summary: Now that you have built it by hand, learn the tool everyone actually uses.

lessons.title: Trees, forests, and gradient boosting
lessons.summary: Decision trees to random forests to XGBoost and LightGBM — still the champions on tabular data.

lessons.title: Feature engineering
lessons.summary: Encoding, missing data, and data leakage — the number one bug in real-world machine learning.

lessons.title: Clustering
lessons.summary: k-means, hierarchical clustering and DBSCAN: finding structure with no labels at all.

lessons.title: PCA and dimensionality reduction
lessons.summary: Where the linear algebra from Phase 1 pays off spectacularly, and eigenvectors finally earn their keep.

lessons.title: Capstone: end to end
lessons.summary: A real, messy dataset from raw file to evaluated model, with every decision written down and justified.

phases.title: Deep Learning
phases.subtitle: build the engine before you drive it
phases.blurb: You will write your own automatic differentiation engine — roughly 150 lines that explain the whole of PyTorch — and train a network on it before touching a framework.
phases.milestone: An autograd engine you wrote yourself, training a network you designed yourself.

lessons.title: The perceptron, and why linear models fail
lessons.summary: XOR: the four data points that stalled an entire field for a decade.

lessons.title: Multi-layer networks
lessons.summary: Activations, hidden layers, and the universal approximation theorem in plain language.

lessons.title: Backpropagation by hand
lessons.summary: Derive it on a three-neuron network, on paper, until there is no magic left in it.

lessons.title: Build an autograd engine
lessons.summary: The crown jewel of this phase. A computation graph, a backward pass, and everything PyTorch does, in miniature.

lessons.title: Train a network on your own engine
lessons.summary: Your code, your gradients, a real classification problem, and a loss curve that goes down.

lessons.title: PyTorch
lessons.summary: Tensors, autograd, nn.Module and the canonical training loop — now with nothing left to take on faith.

lessons.title: Optimisers
lessons.summary: SGD, momentum, RMSProp, Adam — and precisely what problem each one was invented to fix.

lessons.title: Making deep networks trainable
lessons.summary: Initialisation, vanishing and exploding gradients, batch normalisation and layer normalisation.

lessons.title: Regularisation in deep learning
lessons.summary: Dropout, weight decay, early stopping and augmentation — keeping a large model honest.

lessons.title: Convolutional networks
lessons.summary: Build one from scratch, understand what a filter learns, then classify real images.

lessons.title: Transfer learning
lessons.summary: Why almost nobody trains from scratch any more, and how to fine-tune responsibly.

lessons.title: Sequence models
lessons.summary: RNNs and LSTMs, and a precise account of why they break on long sequences.

lessons.title: Embeddings
lessons.summary: word2vec, and representation learning as the central idea of modern artificial intelligence.

lessons.title: Training at scale
lessons.summary: GPUs, batching, mixed precision and checkpointing — the engineering that makes big models possible.

phases.title: Transformers and LLMs
phases.subtitle: from attention to a working GPT
phases.blurb: Attention derived rather than memorised, a byte-pair tokeniser you implement yourself, and a small GPT written line by line and trained on a corpus you choose.
phases.milestone: A working GPT you wrote yourself, generating text.

lessons.title: Attention from first principles
lessons.summary: Derived, not memorised. Queries, keys and values as a solution to a problem you will feel first.

lessons.title: Self-attention and multi-head attention
lessons.summary: Why several attention heads beat one, and how position gets encoded into an order-blind architecture.

lessons.title: The transformer block
lessons.summary: Residual connections, normalisation, feed-forward layers, and encoder versus decoder.

lessons.title: Tokenisation
lessons.summary: Implement byte-pair encoding, then discover why so many odd model behaviours start right here.

lessons.title: Build GPT from scratch
lessons.summary: The full architecture, written line by line and trained on a small corpus until it generates text.

lessons.title: Pretraining and scaling laws
lessons.summary: What 'emergence' does and does not mean, and how compute, data and parameters trade off.

lessons.title: Fine-tuning
lessons.summary: Full fine-tuning, LoRA and PEFT, and instruction tuning — adapting a model you did not train.

lessons.title: Alignment
lessons.summary: RLHF and DPO: how a text predictor becomes something you can hold a conversation with.

lessons.title: Inference
lessons.summary: Sampling, temperature, top-k and top-p, the KV cache, and quantisation.

lessons.title: Embeddings, vector search and RAG
lessons.summary: Retrieval done properly rather than cargo-culted — and this is where lesson 1.1 comes back around.

lessons.title: Evaluations
lessons.summary: The most underrated skill in applied AI, and the one that separates demos from products.

lessons.title: Agents and tool use
lessons.summary: The current frontier: planning, tool calling, and where it genuinely does not work yet.

phases.title: Production and Specialisation
phases.subtitle: models that survive contact with users
phases.blurb: A trained model is roughly ten percent of a machine learning product. This phase covers the other ninety, then you choose a direction to go deep in.
phases.milestone: A model you built, deployed, monitored, and can reason about when it degrades.

lessons.title: Serving and inference in production
lessons.summary: Latency, throughput, cost, batching and the tradeoffs nobody mentions in tutorials.

lessons.title: Monitoring and drift
lessons.summary: Models decay silently. Detecting it, measuring it, and deciding when to retrain.

lessons.title: Reproducibility and experiment tracking
lessons.summary: Versioning data, code and weights so that a result from six months ago can be rebuilt.
